items.name: Celery
items.description: Celery is used in food in various forms, including celery sticks, leaves, seeds and root (celeriac).

items.name: Cereals containing gluten
items.description: 'Cereals containing gluten' includes wheat, which is a common cause of food allergy.

items.name: Crustaceans
items.description: Crustaceans include crab, lobster, crayfish, and prawns.

items.name: Egg
items.description: Egg can be found in a wide range of foods including cakes, pastries, desserts, meat products, mayonnaise, and many more.

items.name: Fish
items.description: Fish allergy refers to fish that have fins such as cod, plaice, haddock, herring, trout, salmon and tuna.

items.name: Lupin
items.description: The lupin is well-known as a popular garden flower. The seeds from certain lupin species are also cultivated as food.

items.name: Milk
items.description: Cow's milk is used to make many foods including butter, cheese, cream, yogurt and more.

items.name: Molluscs
items.description: Molluscs include mussels, oysters, scallops, snails, squid, octopus and many more.

items.name: Mustard
items.description: Mustard plants have seeds that can be white, yellow, brown or black. They can be used to make different types of mustard.

items.name: Tree nuts
items.description: Tree nuts include almonds, Brazil nuts, cashew nuts, hazelnuts, walnuts, pecans, pistachios and macadamia nuts.

items.name: Peanuts
items.description: The peanut is a legume and is in the same plant family as peas, beans and lentils.

items.name: Sesame
items.description: Sesame seeds can be black, white, brown or red. Foods made with sesame include tahini, hummus and halvah.

items.name: Soya
items.description: 'Soya' or 'soy' is made from the soya bean, which is a legume. Soya is used to make soy sauce and tofu and is used as an ingredient in many food products.

items.name: Sulphites/Sulphur Dioxide
items.description: Sulphites are preservatives added to food and drinks to extend their shelf life.
